node.title: Re: call sub_function easily (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Sorry, I wasn't quite awake yet, my reply below isn't as relevant to the question as I thought it was... [Athanasius] [id://1230778|is right]: using a hash table is IMO best (don't use eval or symbolic references). And [tybalt89] [id://1230779|showed] how to make an array of coderefs, which is another good option, depending on your requirements (it doesn't allow you to look up stuff by name).

To deference a code reference, one would normally use $coderef->(). It's also possible to say &$coderef() or &$coderef, but the first form is more modern. See [doc://perlreftut], [doc://perlref], and [doc://perlsub].

I'm not sure what you mean by the second part of your question, whether you want to call the subs, or get their original name? If it's the latter:

use Sub::Util qw/subname/; sub foo {} my $test = \&foo; print subname($test); # prints "main::foo"

[mod://Sub::Util] has been in the core since Perl v5.22.
